content_voiceover: This page walks through two practice questions on T-cell and Ph-like ALL. The first asks which statements about early T-cell precursor ALL, or ETP-ALL, are correct. Statement one is true, ETP-ALL is defined immunophenotypically by low CD5, absent CD1a and CD8, with aberrant stem-cell or myeloid marker expression. Statement two is false, because ETP-ALL actually shows more genomic instability than typical T-ALL, not less. Statement three is true, since that low CD5 expression is sometimes subtle and needs direct comparison with normal lymphocytes on flow. Statement four is false, because ETP-ALL is characterized by myeloid-type mutations like FLT3 and RAS, not KMT2A fusions. So statements one and three are correct, giving answer C. The second question covers Ph-like ALL, which makes up about 10 to 15 percent of pediatric ALL and responds poorly to chemo but may respond to tyrosine kinase or JAK inhibitors. All four listed alterations, IGH-CRLF2, ABL-class fusions, JAK2 rearrangements, and EPOR rearrangements, are genuine Ph-like drivers, so the answer is E, all of the above.
keypoints: ETP-ALL: low CD5, no CD1a/CD8, stem cell/myeloid markers
ETP-ALL has MORE genomic instability, not less
ETP-ALL driven by FLT3/RAS mutations, not KMT2A fusions
Ph-like ALL drivers: CRLF2, ABL-class, JAK2, EPOR
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the ETP-ALL immunophenotype, low CD5, no CD1a, no CD8, plus stem cell or myeloid markers. It carries more genomic instability than typical T-ALL, driven by FLT3 and RAS mutations rather than KMT2A fusions. And for Ph-like ALL, know all four alteration classes, CRLF2 rearrangements, ABL-class fusions, JAK2 rearrangements, and EPOR rearrangements, since these guide TKI or JAK inhibitor selection.
